name: Cayman Islands
prevalence_note: The Royal Cayman Islands Police Service, together with the Cayman Government, has issued repeated public advisories about SMS phishing posing as the Postal Service and demanding customs fees.
cross_border_note: Cayman (+1-345) is in the NANP, so +1 smishing waves from North America and the wider Caribbean blend in with local numbers.

scams.name: Fake Cayman Postal Service customs text
scams.name_en: SMS posing as Cayman Islands Postal Service demanding customs fees via a link
scams.signals_en: A text claims the Cayman Islands Postal Service is holding a parcel until customs fees are paid online.
scams.legit_en: RCIPS and the Cayman Government say the Postal Service does not collect customs by text-message link.
bait_tactics: Ask which post office on Grand Cayman holds it and the customs form number
Say customs is always paid at the counter with the slip in hand

scams.name: Fake local bank alert by SMS or audio call
scams.name_en: SMS or audio-only call posing as a Cayman financial institution or police asking for banking details

red_flag_keywords.text: verify your transactions via this link

scams.signals_en: A text flags unusual activity on a local bank account and links to a fake verification page, or an audio-only call claims to be the bank or local police and asks for banking data.
scams.legit_en: RCIPS tells the public to ignore such messages and contact their financial institution directly through known channels.
bait_tactics: Ask which branch on Grand Cayman flagged the account and the name of the officer
Say the bank will be phoned on the number printed on the debit card
